newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Rwanda refugees in Zaire say fear to return home.
newsitem.headline: Rwanda refugees in Zaire say fear to return home.

text.p: Rwandan refugees stranded in Zaire said on Wednesday they wanted to go home after months of trekking but feared being imprisoned and accused of taking part in Rwanda's genocide in 1994.
The Hutu refugees also said they doubted the ability of the Rwandan government which took power after the victory of Tutsi-dominated rebels to dispense justice fairly.
"We want to return to Rwanda but we are afraid to go to prison without justice," said Biri Sahinquwe, 22, a student from Rwanda's Gitarama province.

A trickle of refugees arrived on Wednesday at Lula camp seven km (four miles) southwest of Kisangani, joining 17,000 exhausted and malnourished refugees who have built temporary shelters from bamboo and leaves since arriving on Friday.
Male refugees at Lula protested their innocence and said former troops of the Hutu Rwandan army split from the main body of refugees between Ubundu, 100 km (60 miles) south of Kisangani, and Lula.

"I am innocent so if there is justice in Rwanda I want to go back...In Rwanda in 1994 there were inter-ethnic massacres but it would be wrong to call it genocide," said Origene Mbunegaba, 25, from Gikongoro in southwest Rwanda.
An estimated 800,000 Tutsis and moderate Hutus were killed in Rwanda in 1994 and more than two million Hutus fled into exile in Tanzania and Zaire fearing reprisals for the genocide.

More than a million refugees returned home in November and December last year but hundreds of thousands more fled deeper into Zaire from camps in October at the start of a war between Zairean rebels and government troops.
They included former Rwandan Hutu troops and Interahamwe militiamen who had a leading role in the 1994 genocide.
Rebels who seized Kisangani on March 15 have granted aid workers access to the refugees but say the Hutus must return to Ubundu, said Paul Stromberg, a spokesman for the U.N. refugee agency.
Unconfirmed reports spoke of a total of 52 bodies were sighted on a 40-km (25-mile) stretch north of Ubundu, he said.
"Most of the refugees here are middle aged or young and they can walk but the reports from Ubundu are quite disturbing," he said at Lula.
A train carrying food for refugees at Ubundu was prevented from leaving Kisangani on Wednesday after failing to get a final rebel clearance.
The rebels have seized about one quarter of Zaire since October in their war to topple President Mobutu Sese Seko.
